decks.title: Italian for travel
decks.description: A Recollect AI starter deck of 15 Italian words and short phrases for greetings, getting around, and ordering. English meanings include useful context.

cards.back: Good morning; hello during the day.
cards.explanation: A polite greeting. The switch to buonasera varies by place and speaker.

cards.back: Good evening.
cards.explanation: Use as an evening greeting. Buonanotte is usually for saying goodnight when leaving late or going to bed.

cards.back: Goodbye.
cards.explanation: A useful polite farewell for shops, restaurants, and other everyday encounters.

cards.back: Thank you.
cards.explanation: Stress the first syllable and keep the final vowel audible.

cards.back: You're welcome.
cards.explanation: A common response to grazie. In other contexts it can invite someone to go ahead.

cards.back: Please.
cards.explanation: Add it to a request: Un biglietto, per favore.

cards.back: Excuse me.
cards.explanation: A polite way to get one person’s attention, such as before asking for directions.

cards.back: Where.
cards.explanation: Dov’è la stazione? asks where the station is. Dov’è combines dove and è.

cards.back: The bathroom; the toilet.
cards.explanation: Dov’è il bagno? is a useful question when you need to find it.

cards.back: The station.
cards.explanation: Often refers to a railway station. La stazione degli autobus specifies the bus station.

cards.back: A ticket.
cards.explanation: Biglietto can refer to a transport ticket or admission ticket; give the destination or event when buying.

cards.back: Water.
cards.explanation: Acqua naturale is still water; acqua frizzante is sparkling.

cards.back: The bill at a restaurant.
cards.explanation: Il conto, per favore is a short, polite request when you are ready to pay.

cards.back: The price.
cards.explanation: Quanto costa? asks how much one item costs.

cards.back: I don't understand.
cards.explanation: You can soften it with Mi scusi before the phrase.

sources.title: Babilonia Italian Language School — Italiano per viaggiare

decks.title: Everyday Spanish
decks.description: A Recollect AI starter deck of 15 Spanish greetings, polite expressions, and short questions. A small starting point for everyday conversations.

cards.back: Hello; hi.
cards.explanation: The h is silent.

cards.back: Good morning.
cards.explanation: Keep the accent in días.

cards.back: Good afternoon; good evening in some regions.
cards.explanation: The change to buenas noches depends on local custom and the time of year.

cards.back: Good evening; good night.
cards.explanation: Used both to greet someone at night and to say goodbye or wish them a good night.

cards.back: Goodbye.
cards.explanation: The accent marks the stressed final syllable.

cards.back: See you later.
cards.explanation: A common farewell even when you have not arranged another meeting.

cards.back: Thank you.
cards.explanation: Muchas gracias adds emphasis: thank you very much.

cards.back: You're welcome.
cards.explanation: Use it after someone thanks you.

cards.back: Please.
cards.explanation: Works at the beginning or end of a request.

cards.back: Excuse me.
cards.explanation: A polite form for addressing one person. Disculpa is the informal form.

cards.back: I'm sorry.
cards.explanation: Use to apologize or express sympathy; disculpe is more useful for politely getting attention.

cards.back: Nice to meet you.
cards.explanation: A short response when someone introduces themselves.

cards.back: I don't understand.
cards.explanation: Entiendo is the first-person form of entender.

cards.back: More slowly.
cards.explanation: Add por favor when asking someone to slow down.

cards.back: The price.
cards.explanation: ¿Cuánto cuesta? asks how much one item costs.

sources.title: Govern de les Illes Balears — Saludos y fórmulas de cortesía
Academia Mexicana de la Lengua — Buena noche o buenas noches

decks.title: French essentials
decks.description: A Recollect AI starter deck of 15 French expressions for polite conversations, cafés, and small everyday requests. Includes brief English meanings.

cards.back: Hello; good morning or good day.
cards.explanation: A daytime greeting. Bonsoir is the usual evening alternative.

cards.back: Good evening.
cards.explanation: Use to greet someone in the evening. Bonne nuit is a wish for a good night, often before bed.

cards.back: Goodbye.
cards.explanation: A standard farewell suitable for everyday polite exchanges.

cards.back: Thank you.
cards.explanation: Merci beaucoup means thank you very much.

cards.back: You're welcome.
cards.explanation: A common reply to merci.

cards.back: Please.
cards.explanation: Use vous with a person you address politely, or with several people. With one familiar person, use s’il te plaît.

cards.back: Excuse me.
cards.explanation: Useful for politely getting attention or apologizing for an interruption.

cards.back: Yes.
cards.explanation: Pronounced roughly like the English word “we.”

cards.back: No.
cards.explanation: The vowel is nasal; avoid adding a strongly pronounced final n.

cards.back: I don't understand.
cards.explanation: Keep the full phrase when learning; informal speech often drops ne.

cards.back: More slowly.
cards.explanation: Add s’il vous plaît when asking someone to slow down.

cards.back: Please repeat.
cards.explanation: The verb uses the polite or plural vous form.

cards.back: The price.
cards.explanation: Combien ça coûte ? asks how much something costs.

cards.back: The bill at a café or restaurant.
cards.explanation: L’addition, s’il vous plaît is a short request when you are ready to pay.

cards.back: Some water.
cards.explanation: De l’eau, s’il vous plaît is a simple request for water.

sources.title: Université libre de Bruxelles MultiGram — S’il te plaît / S’il vous plaît

decks.title: Japanese greetings & essentials
decks.description: A Recollect AI starter deck of 15 Japanese greetings and useful everyday words. Japanese fronts have English meanings and pronunciation hints.

cards.back: Hello; good afternoon.
cards.hint: konnichiwa
cards.explanation: A daytime greeting; the final は is pronounced “wa.”

cards.back: Good morning.
cards.hint: ohayō gozaimasu
cards.explanation: This is the polite form; ohayō is more casual.

cards.back: Good evening.
cards.hint: konbanwa
cards.explanation: The final は is pronounced “wa.”

cards.back: Good night, when going to bed.
cards.hint: oyasuminasai
cards.explanation: This wishes someone rest rather than greeting them on arrival in the evening.

cards.front: ありがとうございます
cards.back: Thank you.
cards.hint: arigatō gozaimasu
cards.explanation: A polite expression of thanks.

cards.back: Excuse me; sorry.
cards.hint: sumimasen
cards.explanation: Useful for getting attention politely or apologizing for a small inconvenience.

cards.back: Please, when making a request.
cards.hint: onegaishimasu
cards.explanation: Often follows what you want, such as a service or item; it does not replace every English “please.”

cards.back: Yes; an acknowledgment that you are listening.
cards.hint: hai
cards.explanation: In conversation, it does not always signal agreement with everything said.

cards.back: No.
cards.hint: iie
cards.explanation: A direct negative response; people may soften refusals in everyday conversation.

cards.back: I don't understand.
cards.hint: wakarimasen
cards.explanation: Add sumimasen before it to politely signal difficulty following a conversation.

cards.back: One more time; once again.
cards.hint: mō ichido
cards.explanation: Add onegaishimasu to politely ask for a repetition.

cards.back: Slowly; at an unhurried pace.
cards.hint: yukkuri
cards.explanation: In a conversation, yukkuri onegaishimasu asks the speaker to slow down.

cards.back: How much does it cost?
cards.hint: ikura desu ka
cards.explanation: Use when the item you mean is clear from context.

cards.back: Toilet; restroom.
cards.hint: toire
cards.explanation: The word uses katakana, a script often used for loanwords.

cards.back: Water.
cards.hint: omizu
cards.explanation: A polite everyday form of mizu, often used when asking for drinking water.

Japan Foundation — Erin Lesson 6: asking prices

cards.back: A push or pull that can change an object's motion.
cards.hint: Think of an interaction.

cards.back: The rate at which velocity changes over time.
cards.hint: A turn counts too.

cards.back: A measure of how strongly an object resists acceleration.

cards.back: The gravitational force acting on an object.
cards.hint: Think of a bathroom scale.

cards.back: A contact force that opposes sliding or the tendency to slide.

cards.back: An object's mass multiplied by its velocity.

cards.back: The energy an object has because it is moving.

cards.back: Energy stored because of an object's position in a gravitational field.

cards.back: Energy changes form or moves between objects, while the total in an isolated system stays constant.

cards.back: Energy transferred because two objects or regions have different temperatures.

cards.back: Heat transfer through direct interactions between neighboring particles.

cards.back: Heat transfer carried by the movement of a liquid or gas.

cards.back: Heat transfer by electromagnetic waves, which can travel through empty space.
cards.hint: Think of warmth from the Sun.

cards.back: A traveling disturbance that needs matter to carry it.
cards.hint: Think of a vibrating speaker.

cards.back: The third planet outward from the Sun.

cards.back: The eighth planet outward from the Sun.

cards.back: A broad region of icy objects orbiting beyond Neptune.

cards.hint: Think of the cell's edge.

cards.back: The compartment holding most of a eukaryotic cell's DNA.
cards.hint: Think of genetic storage.

cards.back: A structure that assembles proteins using instructions carried by RNA.
cards.hint: Think of a protein workshop.

cards.back: An organelle that converts energy from nutrients into ATP during cellular respiration.
cards.hint: Think of usable cellular energy.

cards.back: An organelle that uses light energy to build sugars through photosynthesis.
cards.hint: Think of a green leaf.

cards.back: An organelle that sorts and packages proteins and lipids for transport.
cards.hint: Think of cellular shipping.

cards.back: A network of protein fibers that supports cell shape and movement.

cards.back: A firm outer layer that supports and protects cells such as those of plants.

cards.back: A particle with no electric charge found in an atomic nucleus.

decks.title: Literary devices
decks.description: A Recollect AI starter for noticing how language creates images, sound, and meaning, with original examples.

cards.back: Describes one thing as another to suggest a meaningful resemblance.
cards.hint: “The hallway was a river of backpacks.”

cards.back: Compares different things explicitly, often using like or as.
cards.hint: “The train moved like a tired beetle.”

cards.back: Gives human qualities or actions to something nonhuman.
cards.hint: “The kettle complained from the stove.”

cards.back: Uses deliberate exaggeration for emphasis or effect.
cards.hint: “I carried a mountain of laundry.”

cards.back: Repeats initial consonant sounds across nearby words.
cards.hint: “Brave birds battered the breeze.”

cards.back: Repeats vowel sounds across nearby words.
cards.hint: Listen to the long vowels in “slow boats float.”

cards.back: Repeats consonant sounds within or at the ends of nearby words.
cards.hint: Listen to the repeated sound in “blank trunk.”

cards.back: Uses words whose sounds imitate what they describe.
cards.hint: Consider the sound of “buzz” or “clang.”

cards.back: Briefly refers to another work, person, event, or cultural reference.
cards.hint: Calling a difficult task “a Herculean effort.”

cards.back: Creates a gap between what is said, expected, or understood and what is actually the case.
cards.hint: A boast about perfect planning meets a forgotten map.

cards.back: Uses sensory language to make an experience vivid.
cards.hint: “Warm bread crackled beneath the knife.”

cards.back: Repeats a word or phrase at the beginnings of successive clauses or lines.
cards.hint: “We waited at dawn. We waited at dusk.”

cards.back: Carries a sentence or phrase across a poetic line break without a completing pause.
Tells a story whose characters or events also convey a broader layer of meaning.
cards.hint: A journey may also represent a moral struggle.

cards.back: Directly addresses someone absent or something unable to respond.
cards.hint: “O stubborn moon, keep me company.”

decks.title: Logical fallacies
decks.description: A Recollect AI starter for spotting weak arguments, with short examples and reminders that context matters.

cards.back: Rejects an argument by attacking an irrelevant trait of the person making it.
cards.hint: “Ignore her proposal; her haircut is ridiculous.”

cards.back: Misrepresents an argument to attack an easier version.
cards.hint: A request for less homework becomes “You oppose learning.”

cards.back: Treats a restricted set of choices as exhaustive without justification.
cards.hint: “Either agree with every rule or leave the club.”

cards.back: Claims one step will trigger an extreme chain of consequences without adequate support.
cards.hint: One late assignment supposedly guarantees total academic collapse.

cards.back: Draws a broad conclusion from too little or unrepresentative evidence.
cards.hint: Two rude visitors supposedly describe an entire country.

cards.back: Uses the conclusion, directly or indirectly, as support for itself.
cards.hint: “This rule is right because it is the correct rule.”

cards.back: Claims something is true because it hasn’t been disproved, or false because it hasn’t been proved.
cards.hint: “Nobody disproved my guess, so it must be true.”

cards.back: Assumes an earlier event caused a later one merely because it came first.
cards.hint: A new pen supposedly caused yesterday’s exam success.

cards.back: Diverts attention to an irrelevant issue instead of addressing the argument.
cards.hint: A question about bus delays gets an unrelated parking speech.

cards.back: Dismisses a claim by alleging hypocrisy rather than evaluating its reasons.
cards.hint: “Your advice cannot be right; you ignore it yourself.”

cards.back: Treats widespread belief or popularity as sufficient proof that a claim is true.
cards.hint: “Everyone shares that rumor, so it must be accurate.”

cards.back: Treats an authority’s opinion as decisive despite lacking relevant expertise or reliability.
cards.hint: A famous singer is offered as proof about bridge engineering.

cards.back: Switches a key word’s meaning during an argument.
cards.hint: “Light” can mean low weight or visible radiation.

cards.back: Assumes a whole must have a property because its individual parts have it.
cards.hint: Each tile is light, so the entire shipment must be light.

cards.back: Draws a conclusion from a comparison despite differences relevant to that conclusion.
cards.hint: Two things look alike, but does that support the claim?

decks.title: Statistics essentials
decks.description: A Recollect AI starter for describing data and interpreting evidence, including common traps around correlation and p-values.

cards.back: The sum of numerical values divided by how many values there are.
cards.hint: Imagine sharing the total equally.

cards.back: The middle ordered value, or the average of the two middle values when the count is even.
cards.hint: Sort the numbers before finding the center.

cards.back: The value or values occurring most frequently in a data set.
cards.hint: Can a data set have more than one?

cards.back: The largest value minus the smallest value.
cards.hint: Focus on the two extremes.

cards.back: A measure of spread based on squared deviations from the mean.
cards.hint: Squaring prevents positive and negative deviations from cancelling.

cards.back: The square root of variance, measuring spread in the original units.
cards.hint: Unlike variance, it can be stated in centimeters or seconds.

cards.back: The complete group of individuals or items a study concerns.
A subset of a population selected for study.
cards.hint: A poll asks some people rather than everyone.

cards.back: A numerical characteristic of a population.
cards.hint: Distinguish the whole group from the observed subset.

cards.back: A numerical summary calculated from sample data.
cards.hint: A poll’s average is an estimate, not the population value.

cards.back: Pearson’s correlation measures the direction and strength of a linear relationship between two numerical variables.
cards.hint: A curved relationship can be strong even when this is near zero.
cards.explanation: Correlation alone does not establish that one variable causes the other.

cards.back: Assuming the null hypothesis and test assumptions, the probability of a result at least as extreme as the observed result.
cards.hint: The probability concerns possible data, not whether a hypothesis is true.

cards.back: A baseline claim about a population or probability model that a statistical test evaluates.
cards.hint: Often a claim of no difference or no effect.
cards.explanation: Failing to reject it does not prove it true.

cards.back: An observation unusually far from the rest of the data.
cards.hint: Check an extreme value before deciding to remove it.

cards.back: A sample selected so every possible group of its size has an equal chance of selection.
cards.hint: Think of a thoroughly mixed draw without replacement.
